claims.value: cube
claims.quote: Simple cuboidal cells form this tubule with prominent microvilli on the luminal surface, forming a brush border.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: microvilli
claims.quote: Simple cuboidal cells form this tubule with prominent microvilli on the luminal surface, forming a brush border.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: brush border
claims.quote: Simple cuboidal cells form this tubule with prominent microvilli on the luminal surface, forming a brush border.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: mitochondria: 3 abundant
claims.quote: These cells actively transport ions across their membranes, so they possess a high concentration of mitochondria in order to produce sufficient ATP.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.quote: Cuboidal epithelial cells, shown in , are cube-shaped with a single, central nucleus.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: round
claims.quote: In simple cuboidal epithelium, the nucleus of the box-like cells appears round and is generally located near the center of the cell.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: central
claims.quote: cuboidal | cube shaped, central nucleus | glands, renal tubules

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: distinct apical and basal membrane surfaces carrying different numbers and types of pumps and channels
claims.quote: The numbers and particular types of pumps and channels vary between the apical and basilar surfaces.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Na+–glucose symport proteins on the apical surface
claims.quote: Both glucose and Na+ bind simultaneously to the same symport proteins on the apical surface of the cell to be transported in the same direction, toward the interstitial space.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Na+/K+ ATPase pumps on the basal surface
claims.quote: The energy to move glucose comes from the Na+/K+ ATPase that pumps Na+ out of the cell on the basal surface.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: aquaporin water channels
claims.quote: Water is also independently reabsorbed into the peritubular capillaries due to the presence of aquaporins, or water channels, in the PCT.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: carbonic anhydrase, mostly inside the cell with a small amount bound to the apical brush border
claims.quote: In the kidney, most of the CA is located within the cell, but a small amount is bound to the brush border of the membrane on the apical surface of the cell.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: The microvilli of its brush border give it a large surface area for absorbing and secreting solutes such as Na+, Cl– and glucose.
claims.quote: These microvilli create a large surface area to maximize the absorption and secretion of solutes (Na+, Cl–, glucose, etc.), the most essential function of this portion of the nephron.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Because it actively transports ions across its membranes, it is packed with mitochondria that make enough ATP to power that work.
claims.quote: These cells actively transport ions across their membranes, so they possess a high concentration of mitochondria in order to produce sufficient ATP.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: More substances cross its membranes than anywhere else in the nephron, with amino acids and glucose moved by symporters together with Na+.
claims.quote: More substances move across the membranes of the PCT than any other portion of the nephron. Many of these substances (amino acids and glucose) use symport mechanisms for transport along with Na+.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Na+/K+ ATPase pumps on its basal surface move Na+ out of the cell, supplying the energy that drives glucose transport through it.
claims.quote: The energy to move glucose comes from the Na+/K+ ATPase that pumps Na+ out of the cell on the basal surface.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: It reclaims about 67 percent of the water, Na+ and K+ entering the nephron and almost all of the filtered glucose, amino acids and vitamins.
claims.quote: About 67 percent of the water, Na+, and K+ entering the nephron is reabsorbed in the PCT and returned to the circulation. Almost 100 percent of glucose, amino acids, and other organic substances such as vitamins are normally recovered here.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: Aquaporin water channels in the PCT let water be reabsorbed into the peritubular capillaries.
claims.quote: Water is also independently reabsorbed into the peritubular capillaries due to the presence of aquaporins, or water channels, in the PCT.

source.citation: Clark MA, Douglas M, Choi J (2018). Biology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: A Na+/H+ antiporter releases H+ into the lumen while taking back Na+, recycling hydrogen ions so that bicarbonate can be recovered.
claims.quote: At the same time this is occurring, a Na+/H+ antiporter excretes H+ into the lumen, while it recovers Na+. Note how the hydrogen ion is recycled so that bicarbonate can be recovered.

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: By actively secreting H+ into the forming urine as Na+ is reabsorbed, these cells help the body get rid of excess acid and raise blood pH.
claims.quote: The cells of the PCT actively secrete H+ into the forming urine as Na+ is reabsorbed. The body rids itself of excess H+ and raises blood pH.

source.section: 25.9 Regulation of Fluid Volume and Composition
source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.

claims.value: The PCT is a target of parathyroid hormone, which stimulates the conversion of calcidiol into calcitriol, the active form of vitamin D, there.
claims.quote: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) is an 84-amino acid peptide produced by the parathyroid glands in response to decreased circulating Ca++ levels. Among its targets is the PCT, where it stimulates the hydroxylation of calcidiol to calcitriol (1,25-hydroxycholecalciferol, the active form of vitamin D).

source.citation: Betts JG, Young KA, Wise JA, Johnson E, Poe B, Kruse DH, Korol O, Johnson JE, Womble M, DeSaix P (2022). Anatomy and Physiology 2e. OpenStax.
